Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"78086 The SPC and the additional amount for severe disability will have to be reviewed where the
person is in temporary residential care beyond 28 days and the payability of DLA ceases.


Example


Malcolm and Wendy are married and live together in the same household. Both Malcolm and Wendy get

DLA and CA, or UC that includes the carer element is not in payment. There are no non-dependants.
Higher rate EASD is in payment. Malcolm goes into temporary residential care for 6 weeks.


They are assessed as a couple and the higher rate EASD continues in payment however after 4 weeks
Malcolm’s DLA payments cease and the EASD is withdrawn


Note: The lower rate EASD is not appropriate as there is no facility to treat DLA as in payment for these
periods of respite care.

Concept role: dwp:Applicability.","text":"A limited disregard for the residence condition of the Pension Credit severe-disability additional amount, not a finding that a person is absent from the household for every purpose. Assess normal residence separately. The captured DMG 78077 categories are: a person aged under 18; a person receiving source-defined “AA”, highest- or middle-rate DLA care, standard- or enhanced-rate PIP or ADP daily living, or AFIP; a person certified as blind or severely sight impaired by a consultant ophthalmologist or treated as such; a person living with the claimant to care for the claimant or partner who is engaged by a charitable or voluntary organisation which charges the claimant or partner for their services; that carer’s partner; and a source-defined qualifying young person, or a child for Child Benefit purposes. DMG 78008 limits treated blindness to 28 weeks after regained eyesight and no longer being certified. A voluntary organisation is non-profit and is not a public authority or local authority. Named young-person definitions have age, education, training, benefit-receipt and interruption conditions; neither education alone nor being under 20 is enough. DMG 78078(1) requires first joining the household to care for the claimant or partner, with the claimant or partner satisfying the additional-amount conditions immediately beforehand, and applies only for the first 12 weeks after joining. Its commercial-payment route concerns a person who is not a close relative: payment liability runs either from that person to the claimant or partner for occupation of their dwelling, or from the claimant or partner to that person for occupation of that person’s dwelling; it also covers membership of that person’s household. DMG 78079 requires legal liability and a payment broadly comparable to a lodger’s similar accommodation and facilities. The joint-occupation route requires co-ownership or joint liability to the same landlord, with its non-close-relative condition and the person’s-partner branch. The close-relative exception requires satisfying DMG 78078(3) or (4) as well as the timing condition: the claimant or partner’s co-ownership or joint liability must have arisen before 11 April 1988 or, if later, on or before first occupation; the note uses the right-to-occupy date, not a later moving-in date. Close relative has the captured legal, adoptive and half-sibling meanings. DMG 78080’s registered shared-lives route must retain the accommodation/support and commercial licence conditions and the exclusion where other people cannot be ignored; its completed example is not a general award rule or a current rate. Memo 02/25 paragraph 15 adds Pension Age Disability Payment to the ignored-person benefit list from 21 October 2024, separately from the memo’s claimant/partner and housing-deduction propositions. The dated statutory paragraph 2 also contains Scottish Adult Disability Living Allowance wording requiring separate legal reconciliation; this concept does not consolidate it. Receipt conditions need the full DMG 78060 continuation: its partner-patient item must not be transferred automatically to a third person. Residence, receipt and component, age, care arrangements, relationship, liability and relevant dates remain unknown until evidenced. No staff question establishes these facts or that this component is Concept role: dwp:Applicability.","text":"Source-bounded navigation through DMG 78065–78076, separate from ignoring a person’s presence under 78077–78080 and from deciding whether partners remain one household. Normal residence is where a person usually lives: exceptional visits or absences are disregarded, and temporary absence does not itself change the normal home. DMG 78067 requires factual consideration of time, frequency, permanence, intentions, circumstances, degree of sharing, services, other accommodation and liabilities. An address, university term or overnight stay alone does not settle that assessment. Sharing only a bathroom, lavatory or communal area, or separate legal payment liabilities to the same landlord, has the captured sharing exceptions. Kitchen sharing can exist without entering or using it when personal items are stored or meals prepared there; merely passing through to a self-contained flat is different.
